- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows gradual upward trend but true outcome spikes sharply, reduce forecast slope after spike; avoid over-anticipation.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is rising, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture peak; add 1–3% buffer to forecast peak.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift to positive after low sentiment, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 1–2 days.
- If forecast is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows strong downward correction, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in stability.
